players.product: Formulated epoxy resins for AI semiconductors: liquid molding compound (LMC) and advanced sheet molding compound (a-SMC) encapsulants (Nagase ChemteX)

quarterly_data.quarter: Nagase & Co. results briefing Q&A: FY2026 First Quarter Financial Briefing Q&A (08-05-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Senior Executive Officer Kamada (results briefing Q&A): at the company's largest LMC customer, a semiconductor manufacturer, the investment to expand back-end production capacity, which had been the bottleneck for semiconductors used in generative AI, was completed earlier this fiscal year; LMC (liquid epoxy molding compound) shipment volume has increased to more than 1.5 times the previous year's level. Management says this is not a temporary spike in spot demand but based on a strong customer forecast, expects the high level of shipments and profitability to be sustained beyond Q2, and, based on customers' forecasts, expects growth to stabilize at a low double-digit annual rate continuing through around 2030; the company is prepared to accommodate this growth, including production capacity.
quarterly_data.figure: LMC shipments more than 1.5 times the previous year; low double-digit annual growth expected through around 2030

quarterly_data.quarter: Nagase & Co. results briefing Q&A: FY2026 First Quarter Financial Briefing Q&A (08-05-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Senior Executive Officer Kamada (results briefing Q&A) on a-SMC production: the Harima Plant has been fully equipped with mass-production facilities and is prepared for full-scale commercial mass production; the company will invest to double existing a-SMC capacity within this fiscal year and, by around spring of FY2027, complete additional investments expanding capacity to three times the current level, ahead of the full-scale demand expansion expected in 2028. Investment amounts are not disclosed for competitive and customer-confidentiality reasons.
quarterly_data.figure: a-SMC capacity to double within this fiscal year; three times current level by around spring of FY2027

quarterly_data.quarter: Nagase & Co. results briefing Q&A: FY2026 First Quarter Financial Briefing Q&A (08-05-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Senior Executive Officer Kamada (results briefing Q&A): a-SMC is not a replacement for LMC but a new encapsulant for high-performance IC package substrates; after several years of development it has been recognized by end users as essential for energy efficiency and performance in cutting-edge semiconductors and generative AI, small-scale production began this fiscal year, the project is expected to move to the mass-production phase in the latter half of 2027 with full-scale revenue contributions anticipated in 2028, and management is confident a-SMC has the potential to become a new pillar of growth on a scale comparable to LMC.
quarterly_data.figure: Mass production expected in the latter half of 2027; full-scale revenue contribution in 2028

quarterly_data.quarter: Nagase & Co. results briefing Q&A: FY2026 First Quarter Financial Briefing Q&A (08-05-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Management (results briefing Q&A) on other Electronics products: Nagase ChemteX epoxy sheet materials for SAW filters, used mainly in mid- to low-end smartphones in China, are expected to see a revenue decline of around 20% to 30% this fiscal year as the global memory shortage and demand decline from price increases weigh, fully offset in Q1 by LMC. CMP slurry handled by the trading division is expected to exceed the previous fiscal year. In electronics trading, mature semiconductors of 28 nm and above account for roughly 90% of the Chinese market, with moves in China to double production capacity by 2030, and major customers in South Korea and Taiwan continue large-scale investments, primarily in generative AI. The JPY7.6 billion Electronics net sales increase was partly from higher semiconductor-materials trading sales; Director Shimizu: Nagase ChemteX itself steadily increased profits on high-growth products such as LMC, while the combined profits of the other manufacturing subsidiaries (Pac Tech Group bumping services, Nagase Circrea TMAH recycling) were largely unchanged year on year, so the overall increase in profits for the electronics segment amounted to JPY700 million; Pac Tech maintained stable results in line with the same period last year.
quarterly_data.figure: SAW filter epoxy sheet revenue expected down around 20% to 30% this fiscal year; Electronics net sales +JPY7.6 billion

quarterly_data.quarter: Nagase & Co. results briefing Q&A: FY2026 First Quarter Financial Briefing Q&A (08-05-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Management (results briefing Q&A) on the Materials segment and the Middle East: the company used its supplier network to procure alternative chemical products, mainly solvents used as raw materials for paint thinners during a severe shortage in Japan, from China, India, other parts of Asia and the United States; the positive effects of the temporary market surge and substitute procurement, approximately JPY2 billion in Q1, are expected to fade gradually from Q2 on falling prices and customer inventory adjustment, with general-chemicals shipments slowing in H2, while specialty chemicals for semiconductor process materials are expected to keep performing well. Engineering plastics prices are expected to remain stable, general-purpose resin spreads to narrow with naphtha, and Chinese price pressure on general-purpose polycarbonate may require price adjustments; management sees low risk of a significant Q2 profit decline. Director Shimizu: Q1 gross profit reached 28% and operating income 38% of the full-year forecast, with headquarters relocation expenses expected in H2.
quarterly_data.figure: Approximately JPY2 billion Q1 benefit from the market surge and substitute procurement; Q1 operating income 38% of the full-year forecast

quarterly_data.quarter: Nagase & Co. results briefing Q&A: FY2026 First Quarter Financial Briefing Q&A (08-05-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Director Isobe (results briefing Q&A) on the Prinova Group (Life Sciences): the solutions business (customized formulations and blends for premium pet food, energy drinks and women's sports nutrition, mainly in the US and Europe) progressed at roughly 120% of its Q1 target against an expected annual growth of around 10%; the nutrition business has secured a substantial number of new orders and the company is confident of full-year profitability; utilization at the Utah plant has risen from around 30% to 40% early on to roughly 60% to 70% today, with spare capacity also at the Tennessee plant; manufacturing accounts for approximately 40% of Prinova's profits. Ocean-freight logistics costs weigh on the trading division (80% of Prinova volume, reliant on imports from China and other countries); pass-through price adjustments are expected to show from Q2 onward.
quarterly_data.figure: Solutions business at roughly 120% of Q1 target; Utah plant utilization roughly 60% to 70%
